note: Hepatic APOC3 knockdown (volanesorsen, olezarsen, plozasiran) for FCS and severe hypertriglyceridaemia: human-APOC3-transgenic mice and monkeys supplied the pharmacology, cynomolgus toxicology the platelet signal, and APOC3 loss-of-function carriers the efficacy rationale.
label: Hypertriglyceridemia (APOC3)

engagement.model: Human APOC3-transgenic mice and rhesus monkeys dosed with ISIS 304801 (volanesorsen)
engagement.note: Human-APOC3 transgenic mice, rats and monkeys showed selective apoC-III knockdown; the same paper's phase I in healthy volunteers already showed dose-dependent apoC-III lowering.
engagement.short: ASO knocks down apoC-III in Tg mice, monkeys
engagement.quote: We demonstrated the selective reduction of both apoC-III and triglyceride in all preclinical pharmacological evaluations.
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level only (AHA full text returned 403). Kept untested per rule 6 even though this paper already juxtaposes the animal knockdown with a healthy-volunteer phase I; the fact fields (subjects=healthy_volunteers, comparison_stated=true) let a re-scorer promote it to 'same' in 2013 if healthy-volunteer comparisons are admitted.

engagement.model: Human APOC3-transgenic mice and rhesus monkeys dosed with ISIS 304801 (volanesorsen)
engagement.note: Three FCS patients: plasma apoC-III fell 71-90%, the knockdown the transgenic mice and monkeys predicted; APPROACH later showed 84%.
engagement.quote: After 13 weeks of study-drug administration, plasma APOC3 levels were reduced by 71 to 90% and triglyceride levels by 56 to 86%.
engagement.reason: apoC-III knockdown matched in FCS patients
engagement.judgement: Abstract-level (NEJM paywalled), so comparison_stated is false even though the authors overlap with Graham 2013. First patient-side comparison is this 3-patient open-label study; the randomized confirmation is APPROACH (Witztum 2019, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1715944, apoC-III -84% at 3 months, registry results first posted 2022-04-13). Magnitude left as direction_only because the transgenic-mouse percent knockdown is in the paywalled full text.

dose.model: Monkey (rhesus / cynomolgus) mg/kg dose-response for apoC-III knockdown
dose.note: Monkey dose-response framed the human phase I range; abstract gives direction only, dose numbers sit in the paywalled full text.
dose.short: Monkey dose-response framed phase I doses
dose.quote: Administration of the human apoC-III antisense drug resulted in dose-dependent reductions in plasma apoC-III, concomitant lowering of triglyceride levels, and produced no clinically meaningful signals in the safety evaluations.
dose.judgement: Abstract-level only. The paper reports dose-response in monkeys and in healthy volunteers side by side, but without the full text I cannot state the mg/kg-to-mg/week relationship, so magnitude is null.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey PK/PD with an inhibitory Emax model
dose.note: EMA accepted monkey Emax modelling that 5 mg/kg/wk gives near-maximal knockdown, supporting the 300 mg/week (~4 mg/kg) clinical dose; direct translation was caveated.
dose.quote: The PD study conducted in the monkey is supportive for a potential therapeutic benefit at 300 mg/kg as well as at a reduced dose level in case of thrombocytopenia.
dose.reason: Monkey Emax model supported clinical dose
dose.judgement: Judgement call. The EPAR (EMA/180717/2019, adopted 28 Feb 2019, p.41) says the monkey exposure-PD relationship 'cannot directly be translated to man' because volanesorsen is optimised for the human transcript, and that doses <10 mg/kg were never tested in monkeys; the applicant bridged with an Emax model. I scored it 'same' because the regulator calls the monkey PD 'supportive' of 300 mg/week and the human dose (~4 mg/kg) sits within 2x of the modelled 5 mg/kg, with source_calls_it=scaling to record the caveat. The quoted sentence contains an EPAR typo ('300 mg/kg' should read 300 mg/week). The clinical dose itself was chosen from human phase 1/2 titration, not from the monkey. Olezarsen (GalNAc) later needed 15-30x lower systemic doses; Alexander 2019 (doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehz209) compares it only to volanesorsen in humans, not to an animal model.

efficacy.model: Human APOC3-transgenic mice and fructose-fed hypertriglyceridaemic rhesus monkeys
efficacy.note: Transgenic mice and fructose-fed monkeys lowered TG with apoC-III knockdown; neither carries the LPL deficiency that defines FCS.
efficacy.short: Tg mice and monkeys lower TG
efficacy.quote: Rodent- and human-specific second-generation antisense oligonucleotides were identified and evaluated in preclinical models, including rats, mice, human apoC-III transgenic mice, and nonhuman primates.
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level only. The human APOC3-transgenic mouse (Ito 1990) predates the class; 2013 is its first published use with an APOC3 ASO. The EPAR (p.41-42) records that TG fell only in hypertriglyceridaemic (fructose-fed) rhesus monkeys and not in normolipidaemic cynomolgus monkeys over 13-39 weeks. The parallel human 'model' is APOC3 loss-of-function carriers (TG&HDL Working Group 2014, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1307095: TG 39% lower, apoC-III 46% lower), which supplied the target rationale rather than a preclinical prediction.

efficacy.model: Human APOC3-transgenic mice and fructose-fed hypertriglyceridaemic rhesus monkeys
efficacy.note: TG fell 56-86% in three LPL-deficient FCS patients, matching the transgenic-mouse direction; the LPL-independent mechanism was confirmed in mice only afterwards (Gordts 2016).
efficacy.quote: During the study, all patients had a triglyceride level of less than 500 mg per deciliter (5.7 mmol per liter) with treatment.
efficacy.reason: TG fell in FCS patients as predicted
efficacy.judgement: Abstract-level (NEJM paywalled). The models predicted TG lowering via LPL disinhibition; FCS patients lack LPL yet responded, so the direction matched for a reason the models had not isolated. Gordts 2016 (doi:10.1172/JCI86610) then showed in LPL-null mice that the ASO lowers TG through LDLR/LRP1 clearance, reverse-translating the patient result. Randomized confirmation: APPROACH (Witztum 2019, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1715944, TG -77% vs +18% placebo, registry results 2022-04-13) and olezarsen Balance (Bergmark 2024, doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2400201, 80 mg: -43.5 points vs placebo, pancreatitis rate ratio 0.12, registry results 2025-03-06). Volanesorsen was approved by EMA (May 2019) and refused by FDA (CRL Aug 2018) on safety, not efficacy.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology (2'-MOE ASO class)
safety.note: Pivotal paper reported monkey tolerability and no meaningful phase I safety signal; platelets are not mentioned in the abstract.
safety.quote: We also showed that inhibition of apoC-III was well tolerated and not associated with increased liver triglyceride deposition or hepatotoxicity.
safety.judgement: Abstract-level only; whether the 2013 full text discusses monkey platelet counts is unverified.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey platelet counts (102 2'-MOE ASOs, >2,200 monkeys)
safety.note: Class-wide NHP-to-human platelet comparison, but the human arm was a diabetes ASO (ISIS 404173), not an APOC3 drug; monkeys overpredicted severe drops.
safety.short: Class platelet signal matched, other ASO
safety.quote: Based on these data, the consistent, self-limiting PLT reduction seen in NHP may translate to humans, but these changes appear to be of limited clinical significance.
safety.judgement: Scored 'other' because the only published model-vs-patient platelet comparison in 2017 is for a 2'-MOE ASO against a different target (ISIS 404173, type 2 diabetes phase 2, 62 patients at 200 mg/wk: no platelet count <75K). The same abstract adds that 'NHPs appear to overpredict the incidence of sporadic PLT <50K cells/muL compared to humans' - a direction the volanesorsen experience would reverse two years later. Ionis-authored; abstract read in full, body not.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 13- and 39-week toxicology of volanesorsen
safety.note: Monkeys showed thrombocytopenia (two deaths at 12 and 20 mg/kg/wk); APPROACH: 47% of patients <100,000/uL, 6% <25,000; hazard matched, incidence not predicted.
safety.short: Monkey thrombocytopenia matched; FDA still refused
safety.quote: The main hazard identified in animals is a reduction in platelet count leading to thrombocytopenia, which has also been observed in humans in the clinical trials.
safety.judgement: Judgement call between 'same' and 'contra'. The EPAR (EMA/180717/2019, p.42-43) states the monkey finding 'is considered a clinically relevant effect as thrombocytopenia was also observed in clinical trials', lists in its 39-week cynomolgus study (0-3-6-12-20 mg/kg/wk) 'sporadic cases of very low PLT' from 6 mg/kg/wk and one thrombocytopenia death each at 12 and 20 mg/kg/wk, and reports in APPROACH (CS6) 15/32 (46.9%) confirmed nadir <100,000/mm3 and 2 (6.3%) <25,000/mm3 on volanesorsen vs 0 on placebo. So the model flagged the hazard: 'same', with source_calls_it=match. What it did not predict is incidence: Henry 2017 had concluded monkeys overpredict severe drops, yet volanesorsen produced grade 4 thrombocytopenia in 2/33 FCS patients and <100K in roughly half; no monkey study reproduced that frequency (magnitude=direction_only). FDA issued a complete response (Aug 2018, letter not public) after a 12-8 EMDAC vote; the 10 May 2018 transcript (fda.gov/media/131530, p.94-95) records FDA's count of 55% <100,000 and 2 <25,000 and Ionis's statement that 3-month monkey platelet-function tests showed 'no effect on platelet function'. If a revised rule scores incidence misses as contradiction, re-score this cell 'contra'. Witztum 2019 (doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1715944) carries the same numbers: 'No patients in the placebo group had platelet counts below 100,000 per microliter, whereas 15 of 33 patients in the volanesorsen group had such levels, including 2 who had levels below 25,000 per microliter.' Olezarsen (GalNAc, 50-80 mg q4w) showed no platelet signal in its phase 1/2a (Alexander 2019: 'there were no changes in platelet counts') and Balance 2024 abstract reports no thrombocytopenia; FDA approved it Dec 2024. That is consistent with the monkey class model (Zanardi 2021, doi:10.1124/jpet.120.000222: GalNAc conjugation widens the platelet margin via potency), so no status change was added for 2024.
